sections.html:
Spokane lies along the Spokane River in eastern Washington, roughly 18 miles from Idaho and 229 miles east of Seattle. An estimated 230,783 people lived here on July 1, 2025, a gain of 0.8 percent over the April 2020 base. Homeowners hold 58.8 percent of households, and the median home is valued at $363,500. A citywide figure tells you little about one block, so look at recent sales on your own street.

For anyone whose house or street was hit, this is the first thing to sort out. The Old Trails Fire in early August 2026 destroyed more than 600 buildings, and Spokane has been running a recovery program for burned and damaged properties ever since.

Help available through the city's wildfire page and the county's recovery pages includes:

  • A free asbestos survey, on request, for owners of properties the Old Trails Fire affected.
  • A year of free application completeness screening from Permavia for residential rebuilding permits. It is optional and does not replace the city's own review.
  • Spokane County's Demolition and Rebuilding FAQ and Next Steps FAQ.
  • A phone line: 311 inside the city, or 509.755.CITY (2489) from elsewhere, Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.

People who lost a house or own a damaged one often debate rebuilding versus selling the lot or the shell. Before signing anything, get your insurer's answer in writing on how a sale affects an open claim, and ask the county assessor how the damage changes your assessed value.

Buyers of fire-area property may ask for the survey results, the permit history and any insurance paperwork. Keep these together in one folder so you can share them quickly and show a buyer how the house reached its current condition.

Location shapes value. Downtown and Riverside are the business core, South Hill rises to the south, and Browne's Addition, west of downtown, is a National Historic District of Queen Anne and Craftsman mansions. Hillyard, in the northeast, started in 1892 around the Great Northern Railway yard. East Central, the University District and West Central complete the older core, and 18 National Register historic districts exist citywide.

Living in one? Before you repaint, re-side or replace windows to prepare for a sale, ask city planning staff whether exterior changes need design review. Spokane Public Schools (District 81) covers most of the city, and the Mead School District serves parts of north Spokane County beyond city limits.

Historic status can help or hinder. Some buyers seek out an older home with period detail, while others worry about rules for renovation. Know which group your neighborhood attracts, and describe the house with that in mind.

sections.h2: Permits to close out before you list
sections.html:
Sort out permits with the city before you list. Spokane handles permits through its Accela Citizen Access portal. The Development Services Center is open in person from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, and from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Wednesday.

  • Look up the permit history for projects you did or inherited: a finished basement, a new deck, a replaced water heater.
  • Ask staff how to resolve an expired or open permit, ideally before a buyer's inspector spots it.
  • Use only the city's portal to pay. Fake permit invoices are circulating, and the city never requests payment through emailed wire instructions.

For lot size and the legal description that belongs on the deed, check the county's parcel information search, which also shows tax history and assessed value.

If you hold a permit for fire-related work, bring that file to the first conversation with any buyer. A clear paper trail shows what was repaired and when.

Under Washington law the excise tax on a real estate sale normally falls on the seller. It is payable to the Spokane County Treasurer, because that is the county where the property sits, and it is due on the sale date even if the deed has not yet been recorded. The state's first two tiers are 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent through $1,525,000. For sales starting January 1, 2027 the thresholds shift to $551,000 and $1,551,000. A local share is added, so get the full rate from the treasurer before you estimate what you will net.

Interest begins if the tax is unpaid one month after the sale, at the 6 percent rate the Department of Revenue lists for 2026,, and the debt can turn into a lien.

For most house sales the buyer is owed a completed seller disclosure statement within five business days of both parties signing the contract. After that the buyer has three business days to rescind, unless you agree otherwise under RCW 64.06.020. The form probes structure, roof, systems, and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, and a buyer is free to waive it.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense
sections.html:
Consider cash when time or the house's condition counts for more than a bit of extra price. An agent listing means prep work, open houses and a wait for the buyer's lender. A cash buyer takes the place as it is and may close on a day that suits you. That helps with fire damage, an inherited property, or a rental where the tenant is difficult.

Ask any Spokane bidder to commit these terms on paper:

  • The total price, plus who covers excise tax and recording fees.
  • A closing date and the name of the title or escrow firm.
  • Whether repairs, leftover belongings and open permits stay with the house.
  • An expiration for the offer, and what becomes of any earnest money.

Run the numbers against a listing that nets you the price minus repairs, commission and carrying costs. If the cash offer is lower, that gap pays for skipping the work and the waiting.

Once you say yes, a title company combs through the public record while escrow holds the paperwork. Your mortgage balance, if any, is settled from the proceeds. You sign the deed before a notary, the county receives the tax and affidavit, and you are paid after recording.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Spokane?
faqs.a: It depends on your route. Cash has no loan approval to wait on, so it can beat a listing, though title work and the escrow company decide the real closing date.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax on a Spokane sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, in most cases, and the Spokane County Treasurer collects it by the sale date. State tiers begin at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, with a local share added. Ask the treasurer for the combined rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a fire-damaged house in Spokane?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners affected by the August 2026 Old Trails Fire can ask the city for a free asbestos survey, and the county posts demolition and rebuilding guidance. Check with your insurer first about how a sale affects an open claim.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a Spokane buyer a seller disclosure statement?
faqs.a: In most residential sales, yes: a completed form within five business days after the contract is signed. A waiver by the buyer or an exempt transfer changes that. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

faqs.q: Where do I check property tax history for a Spokane house?
faqs.a: The Spokane County parcel information site shows tax history and assessed value. For a payoff or proration at closing, ask the Spokane County Treasurer.
